A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MOCOBO. The complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimization experiments, covering-set examples, an ablation study and in vitro antimicrobial measurements in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, a conflicting-objective rover experiment and algorithm runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The coverage objective, greedy covering-set construction, ECI acquisition, top-q batching, coordinated trust regions and surrogate architecture are retained. The reorganized explanation and newly disclosed parallel marginal-score computation do not establish a changed optimization method.

E1.justification: The existing peptide, molecule, rover and image tasks remain. Appendix A.2.2 adds a distinct rover scenario with three pairwise highly conflicting obstacle courses and two covering trajectories, extending evaluation to an environment where full coverage is impossible.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 2 adds CluSO and uniform random sampling across the eight existing benchmark comparisons. The earlier TuRBO/LOL-BO, ROBOT, MORBO and individually optimized reference comparisons remain. Adding CluSO introduces a directly relevant coverage-optimization competitor.

E3.justification: v2 adds a controlled runtime protocol comparing parallel and serial marginal-score evaluation across N=20 to 2,000,000 and six combinations of K and T. It also specifies settings for the new baselines, including rejection sampling for constrained peptides. Existing BO settings are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained known-partition ablation, Appendix A.2.2 tests behavior when all objectives conflict and illustrates unavoidable trajectory collisions. Appendix A.2.3 adds scaling and parallelization analyses of Algorithm 1. These substantially broaden the examination of applicability and computational efficiency.

E5.justification: The optimization experiments retain 20 replications with standard errors, and the biological assays retain three replicates. The new runtime study explicitly reports 10 repetitions and standard errors in Table A.3; this does not indicate increased replication of existing experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds CluSO and random-sampling curves, runtime measurements and conflicting-objective results. In the new rover scenario, two MOCOBO solutions average 2.932 coverage versus 12.899 for three individually optimized solutions. Earlier peptide tables, wet-lab heatmaps and principal optimization findings are retained.

T1.justification: The NP-hardness reduction, monotonicity/submodularity reasoning, approximation guarantee and complexity claims remain. Appendix A.10 introduces g_t(S) as shorthand and rewrites the existing proof expressions without changing their mathematical substance or assumptions.

C1.justification: v1 claims to introduce coverage optimization and to be the first work considering it. v2 narrows this central novelty claim to the Bayesian optimization literature. The main claims about optimization performance, compact covering sets and antimicrobial activity remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly explains the impossibility of fully covering pairwise conflicting objectives with K<T solutions and interprets the resulting compromises. It also discusses jointly optimizing K in future work. The earlier qualifications about choosing K and misleading image-quality metrics are retained.

D1.justification: v2 discloses parallel marginal-score computation, new-baseline implementation details, hardware, memory use, execution times and total GPU expenditure in Appendices A.2.3 and A.6. These substantially expand practical reproducibility information beyond the retained model and initialization details. Code links remain placeholders.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantive discussion of coverage work by Ding, Li, Lin and Liu, distinguishing differentiable approaches from black-box optimization and acknowledging CluSO as prior black-box coverage work. Appendix A.9 also explicitly disclaims novelty for the NP-hardness proof.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are edited, trust-region explanations are consolidated, and baseline subsection organization changes. Impact and image-quality discussion move into the appendices, while acknowledgments and a checklist are added. Most existing exposition is retained.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. v1 Figure 2 is removed; Figures 4 and 6 are combined into v2 Figure 3. Benchmark plots gain expanded axes and a shared legend, new analysis displays are added, and several retained figures are substantially reduced in size.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves an important positioning and comparison gap: it acknowledges prior coverage research, narrows the novelty claim and evaluates the directly relevant CluSO competitor across the benchmarks. The conflicting-objective experiment and runtime/resource disclosures further clarify applicability and computational feasibility. These gains outweigh reduced legibility in some resized figures, although usable code links remain absent.
